title: CuTe DSL Decorators Overview
critical_patterns: Use @cute.jit to orchestrate GPU work from the CPU
Use @cute.kernel for writing GPU computation with explicit thread/block control
Common pattern: @cute.jit hosts function orchestrates @cute.kernel launch
Nesting @jit functions to launch multiple kernels for complex pipelines
constraints: Python functions cannot directly call @kernel functions
Control flow may not work with preprocessor=False
compressed_summary: CuTe DSL provides two main decorators, @cute.jit and @cute.kernel, for generating optimized code through dynamic compilation. @cute.jit is used for host-side JIT-compiled functions that typically run on the CPU and manage GPU execution, while @cute.kernel is used for defining GPU kernel functions that require explicit grid and block configuration. The preprocessor parameter in both decorators controls the handling of loops and conditionals, with preprocessor=True automatically converting control flow to intermediate representation, which is recommended for most use cases. The no_cache parameter in @cute.jit controls JIT caching behavior, useful for debugging and testing. Kernel functions are launched using the .launch() method, specifying grid and block dimensions, and optionally, cluster dimensions, shared memory size, and CUDA stream. Python functions can call @jit functions directly but cannot call @kernel functions directly; instead, @jit functions can launch @kernel functions. A typical pattern involves using @cute.jit to orchestrate GPU work and @cute.kernel for the actual computation. Common pitfalls include forgetting to use .launch() for kernels, using @kernel for host code, and incorrect control flow handling with preprocessor=False. The documentation encourages using @cute.jit for orchestrating GPU work and preparing data, and @cute.kernel for parallel computation and explicit control over threads and blocks. Advanced usage includes nesting @jit functions to create complex pipelines. Related topics include quick start guides, code generation, and control flow handling.
